hook: A day on Venus is longer than its year
body: Venus takes 243 Earth days to rotate once, but only 225 Earth days to orbit the Sun. So a Venusian day is longer than a Venusian year.

hook: Neutron stars are absurdly dense
body: A single teaspoon of neutron star material would weigh about a billion tons on Earth — roughly as much as a mountain.

hook: There's a planet made partly of glass rain
body: On exoplanet HD 189733b, winds reach 5,400 mph and it likely rains molten glass sideways.

hook: Saturn could float in water
body: Saturn's average density is lower than water's, so if you had a bathtub big enough, the whole planet would float.

hook: The Sun loses 4 million tons every second
body: Nuclear fusion converts about 4 million tons of the Sun's mass into pure energy every second — and it's been doing this for 4.6 billion years.

hook: One day on the Moon lasts about a month
body: Because the Moon rotates so slowly relative to Earth, a single lunar day-night cycle lasts roughly 29.5 Earth days.

hook: There's a giant hexagon storm on Saturn
body: At Saturn's north pole sits a jet stream shaped almost perfectly like a hexagon, wide enough to fit four Earths inside it.

hook: We've explored less of the ocean than space
body: More than 80% of the ocean remains unmapped and unexplored — we have better maps of the Moon and Mars than our own seafloor.

hook: The blue whale's heart is the size of a car
body: A blue whale's heart can weigh around 400 pounds, and its heartbeat can be detected from over a mile away underwater.

hook: There's a jellyfish that's basically immortal
body: Turritopsis dohrnii can revert its cells back to an earlier life stage when stressed or injured, effectively resetting its aging process.

hook: The Mariana Trench could swallow Everest
body: The deepest point of the ocean is nearly 36,000 feet down — if you dropped Mount Everest in, its peak would still be over a mile underwater.

hook: Octopuses have three hearts
body: Two pump blood to the gills, and one pumps it to the rest of the body — and that main heart actually stops beating when they swim.

hook: Your stomach gets an entirely new lining every few days
body: Stomach acid is strong enough to dissolve metal, so your stomach lining regenerates roughly every 3 to 5 days to keep from digesting itself.

hook: You produce about a liter of saliva a day
body: Over an average lifetime, a person produces enough saliva to fill two swimming pools.

hook: Your bones are stronger than steel by weight
body: Pound for pound, bone can withstand more pressure than steel, while being about five times lighter.

hook: You can't tickle yourself
body: Your brain's cerebellum predicts the sensation of your own movement and cancels out the response, which is why self-tickling barely works.

hook: Your nose can remember 50,000 different scents
body: The human olfactory system can distinguish and recall tens of thousands of distinct smells, often tied directly to long-term memory.

hook: Cleopatra lived closer to the Moon landing than the pyramids
body: The Great Pyramid was built around 2560 BC. Cleopatra was born around 69 BC — closer in time to the 1969 Moon landing than to the pyramid's construction.

hook: Oxford University is older than the Aztec Empire
body: Oxford was already teaching students by 1096, while the Aztec Empire wasn't founded until 1428.

hook: The shortest war in history lasted 38 minutes
body: The Anglo-Zanzibar War of 1896 ended in under 40 minutes after British forces bombarded the Sultan's palace.

hook: Napoleon was once attacked by rabbits
body: During a hunting event, thousands of released rabbits swarmed Napoleon's group instead of fleeing, reportedly forcing him to retreat to his carriage.

hook: Ancient Romans used urine as mouthwash
body: Because of its ammonia content, Romans imported urine from Portugal specifically as a teeth-whitening agent.

hook: A group of flamingos is called a flamboyance
body: It's an official collective noun — much like a murder of crows or a parliament of owls.

hook: Elephants can't jump
body: Elephants are the only mammal that physically cannot jump, because their leg structure and body weight don't allow all four feet to leave the ground at once.

hook: A shrimp can punch faster than a bullet leaves a gun
body: The mantis shrimp's claw strike accelerates faster than a .22 caliber bullet, creating a shockwave hot enough to briefly flash light underwater.

hook: Cows have best friends
body: Studies show cows form close social bonds and become measurably more stressed when separated from their preferred companion.

hook: A snail can sleep for three years
body: During extreme heat or drought, some snails enter a dormant state called estivation that can last up to three years.

hook: Your brain can't tell the difference between rejection and physical pain
body: Social rejection activates the same brain regions as physical injury, which is why heartbreak can feel literally painful.

hook: You forget most new information within a day
body: The forgetting curve shows people typically lose over half of new information within 24 hours unless it's actively reviewed.

hook: Multitasking isn't actually real
body: Your brain can't process two conscious tasks simultaneously — it rapidly switches between them, which is why multitasking makes you slower and more error-prone.

hook: Deja vu might be your brain double-checking itself
body: One leading theory suggests deja vu happens when your brain briefly misfires, tagging a new experience as a memory being recalled instead of one being formed.

hook: Bananas are naturally radioactive
body: Bananas contain potassium-40, a radioactive isotope, in small enough amounts that it's completely harmless — but measurable.

hook: Glass is technically still moving
body: Old glass is sometimes thicker at the bottom not because it flows over centuries, but early manufacturing made it uneven — though glass is technically an amorphous solid, not a true liquid.

hook: Hot water can freeze faster than cold water
body: Under certain conditions, this is called the Mpemba effect — scientists still debate the exact reasons why it happens.

hook: Honey never spoils
body: Archaeologists have found 3,000-year-old honey in Egyptian tombs that was still perfectly edible, thanks to its low moisture and natural acidity.

hook: Lightning is hotter than the surface of the Sun
body: A bolt of lightning can reach around 30,000 Kelvin — roughly five times hotter than the Sun's surface.
